lessons.title: GOTO: Jumping Around
intro: So far, programs ran from the first line straight down to END. GOTO changes that: GOTO 40 jumps directly to line 40 and continues from there.
Lines that are jumped over are simply skipped. You can also jump backwards, to a lower line number, and run lines again.
Careful: a GOTO that always jumps backwards creates an endless loop. The program never reaches END.
STOP ends the program immediately, wherever it appears. Unlike END, it can stand anywhere in the program.

exercises.explanation: Line 20 jumps to line 40, so line 30 is skipped. B is never printed.
GOTO followed by a line number jumps to that line.

exercises.prompt: What happens when you run this?
exercises.explanation: Line 20 always jumps back to line 10, so the program never reaches END. That's an endless loop.

exercises.prompt: This program crashes. Which line causes it?
exercises.explanation: Line 20 jumps to line 50, but there is no line 50. GOTO always needs a line that exists.
STOP ends the program right away, so line 30 never runs.

exercises.prompt: In what order are the PRINT lines executed?
exercises.explanation: 10 jumps to 40 (FIRST), 50 jumps back to 20 (SECOND), and 30 jumps to END.

lessons.title: IF…THEN: Decisions
intro: IF lets the program make decisions: IF A > 5 THEN 50 jumps to line 50, but only if A is greater than 5. Otherwise the program simply continues with the next line.
BASIC compares numbers with = (equal), <> (not equal), < (less than), > (greater than), <= (less or equal) and >= (greater or equal).
In the original 1964 BASIC, THEN is always followed by a line number. Commands like THEN PRINT only came in later versions.

exercises.explanation: <> means 'not equal'. Many modern languages write != instead.
4 is not less than 3, so the jump doesn't happen. Line 30 prints A, and line 40 skips over B.

exercises.prompt: Jump to line 50 if A is NOT equal to 0.
X is 5. Which condition is true?
exercises.explanation: >= means 'greater or equal'. 5 is equal to 5, so X >= 5 is true.

exercises.prompt: This line works in later BASICs, but not in 1964. Which one?
exercises.explanation: In the original BASIC, THEN must be followed by a line number, like THEN 50.

options: Without it, SMALL numbers would also print BIG
END needs a GOTO in front of it
exercises.explanation: After printing SMALL, the program would continue to line 50 and also print BIG. GOTO 60 jumps over it.

lessons.title: Counting with Jumps
intro: With IF and GOTO together you can repeat lines on purpose: a counter variable goes up by 1 each round, and IF jumps back until it reaches the target.
This pattern has three parts: start the counter (LET I = 1), change it (LET I = I + 1), and check it (IF I <= 3 THEN ...).
If you forget to change the counter, the condition never becomes false, and you get an endless loop.

exercises.explanation: I starts at 1 and goes up after each PRINT. When I becomes 4, the condition is false and the program reaches END.

exercises.prompt: Make the program count from 1 to 5.
exercises.explanation: The loop repeats as long as I is at most 5, so it prints 1 to 5.

exercises.prompt: Why does this program never stop?
options: I never changes, so I <= 3 is always true
exercises.explanation: There is no LET I = I + 1, so I stays 1 forever and the program keeps jumping back.
Start at 3, print, count down by 1, and jump back as long as C is still above 0.

exercises.prompt: What is the last number this program prints?
exercises.explanation: It prints 2, 4, 8, 16. Then N becomes 32, which is not below 20, so the loop ends.

exercises.prompt: Add up the numbers 1 to 3 in S.
exercises.explanation: Each round adds I to S: 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. This 'running total' pattern is used all the time.
